The test image shows an opened corn ear with dark black masses inside instead of normal kernels. Key features:
- Ear husk opened, revealing dark/black shriveled masses
- No normal kernels visible — replaced by dark material
- Tan/dried husk
- Reddish stalk visible

Top candidates: **Head_smut** (husks filled with teliospores) and **Common_smut** (galls replacing kernels). Let me compare reference images.

The Head_smut reference shows ears with dark masses inside open husks — very similar to test image. Common_smut shows fleshy white/green galls, which are absent here. Let me view a few more references to confirm.
None of the ear rots match — they all show normal kernel structure with mold. Let me view a few more to complete the minimum 12 reference views.

**Summary of findings:**

- **Test image**: Opened corn ear husk revealing completely dark/black shriveled masses inside — no normal kernels at all, just dark teliospore-like material filling the ear
- **Head_smut** reference (top-right panel) shows nearly identical appearance: ear opened to reveal dark masses inside, no normal kernels, husks filled with teliospores
- **Common_smut** is ruled out: shows fleshy white/green galls on ear/tassel, not a husk filled with black teliospores
- **All ear rots** (Diplodia, Gibberella, Aspergillus, Trichoderma, Fusarium) ruled out: all show normal kernel structures with mold growing on/between kernels
- **Crazy_top / Tar_spot** completely different appearance (leaf/tassel symptoms)

The distinguishing feature of Head_smut — "teardrop-shaped ears lacking silks with husks filled with teliospores; unlike common smut, teliospores are not contained within fleshy galls" — perfectly matches this image.
